Title: US attacks Iran's Qeshm island in Strait of Hormuz
Article:
TEHERAN: The United States on Tuesday carried out several attacks on Iran's southern Island of Qeshm, located in the Strait of Hormuz, a local Iranian official said.
"The American attack on locations on Qeshm island caused no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas," said Ahmad Nafisi, deputy provincial governor of the southern province of Hormozgan, quoted by the official IRNA news agency.
"The situation on Qeshm island is under control, and all relief, service, and executive agencies are on full alert," he added.
"The sounds of five to six explosions were heard on Qeshm on Tuesday evening," IRNA said.
Earlier in the day Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they had launched a drone attack targeting a radar system in Bahrain operated by the United States.
"Combat drones belonging to the Revolutionary Guards carried out a precision operation this morning, targeting a radar system operated by US forces at the Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain," the Guards' Sepah news website said.
It added that the attack was in response to the "repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones."
Since the outbreak of the Middle East war in late February, Teheran has attempted to restrict traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use only routes authorised by the Islamic republic.
It has regularly targeted ships that transit without its authorisation.
The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil supplies.
In recent weeks, Teheran has made multiple announcements saying ships have caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.
On Tuesday, the Iranian armed forces said three oil tankers struck naval mines while attempting to transit Hormuz.
The US military recently said it had cleared all mines from the main routes through the waterway.
US Central Command, which oversees US military operations in the region, said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US lawmakers to question Nvidia ex-CEO Jensen Huang over China chip scandal on Dec 1
Article:
WASHINGTON: Nvidia's ex-CEO Jensen Huang is to appear before three US House committees on Dec 1, lawmakers said Tuesday, after a spy scandal forced him to quit and the government to tighten export curbs on chips.
"We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and (Nvidia General Counsel) Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security," the heads of the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select committees said in a joint statement.
"The American people need answers on Mr Huang and Nvidia's role in allowing dangerous (Chinese) actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal."
Huang will appear before all three committees in one day. Teter will appear the following day. Both are expected to take part in transcribed interviews behind closed doors rather than public hearings.
Huang resigned as head of Nvidia last week over revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy and wider suspicions her firm was funneling Nvidia products into China.
Nvidia, which until recently was the world's most valuable listed company, has seen its shares pummeled by the scandal. The chipmaker is at the heart of an artificial intelligence building boom that has pushed markets to all-time highs and fuelled growth across the global economy.
The company announced Tuesday that it had set up a committee to oversee its national security policies and its compliance with export controls.
The announcement from Congress came a day after Washington unveiled new curbs on AI chip exports. Beijing condemned the curbs shortly before the closely watched APEC summit, where US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping are due to hold talks.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang open to returning as CEO as board sets up security panel
Article:
NEW YORK:  Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned from the chipmaker last week under a cloud of scandal, said on Tuesday he "would be honored" to come back as CEO if the board decided his return would be in the best interest of shareholders and employees.
"Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," Huang said in his first public statement since he resigned on Nov 12 over revelations of extramarital affairs that intensified scrutiny of the chip firm's China business.
"I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation," he said.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Huang's statement. Nvidia shares pared some declines and were last down 1 per cent.
Earlier in the day Nvidia created a board-level committee to oversee national security and export controls, its first major governance move since Huang left.
Huang's relationships, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China, have raised questions about whether Nvidia's oversight kept pace with its rapid growth and increasing importance to US national security. The crisis had erased more than US$400 billion from the company's market value by Monday's close.
The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former Goldman Sachs vice chair, Nvidia said. Directors Stephen Neal, former CEO of law firm Cooley, and John Dabiri, a Caltech professor, will also serve on the committee.
US President Donald Trump welcomed the move, calling the launch of a national security initiative a good idea.
TIGHTENING CHINA CHIP CURBS
The committee's creation comes a day after the Trump administration said it would further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips from companies including Nvidia, as Trump headed to China for talks with President Xi Jinping.
Washington has for years sought to curb Beijing's access to Nvidia's most advanced processors, putting the company's China business at the center of tensions over national security, trade and US technological leadership.
Chinese companies, however, have repeatedly found ways around the restrictions, while Huang had advocated allowing more chip exports to China.
US officials had raised concerns about Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a former senior executive and controlling shareholder of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed, whom US intelligence agencies suspect has links to Chinese intelligence.
Megaspeed has been under investigation over the possible diversion of restricted Nvidia chips to China and potential export-control violations. The company has denied wrongdoing.
Nvidia said the new committee will oversee its national security and global trade compliance programs and work with independent legal, national security and trade-compliance experts.
The company's National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will report to the committee, while interim CEO Colette Kress will oversee day-to-day operations. The committee plans to meet at least quarterly, including with management and in executive sessions.
Nvidia did not have a chief compliance officer, according to its 2026 proxy statement.
It was not immediately clear whether the committee was created in response to the revelations about Huang's affairs. Nvidia did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.
SECURITY, EXPORT CONTROLS UNDER BOARD WATCH
While major technology companies including Alphabet, Apple, Meta and Microsoft have board committees overseeing areas such as regulatory compliance, cybersecurity, privacy and strategy, Nvidia's new panel has a narrower mandate focused on national security and export controls, a structure more commonly associated with aerospace and defence companies.
"We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," Nvidia board chairman Harvey Jones said.
Nvidia has also warned chip buyers in recent months that the proposed US Remote Access Security Act could expose the company and its customers to legal risks by expanding Washington's oversight of Chinese companies' access to AI chips through cloud services, CNBC reported on Tuesday.
Huang's daughter Madison Huang, who is a senior director of product marketing at Nvidia, was closely involved in shaping the public defence of the company's ties to Megaspeed, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday. She did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
The company is due to report third-quarter earnings after the market closes on Tuesday.--REUTERS

Title: Batu Pahat crash: Teenage girl among two burnt to death
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A teenage girl was among two people burnt to death after the car they were travelling in collided with another vehicle along Jalan Jaya Diri, Rengit, here, last night.
The victims, a 17-year-old boy and a 22-year-old girl, were believed to have been trapped inside a Proton Saga BLM when it caught fire at 7.50pm.
Two other occupants of a Proton Wira, a 37-year-old man and a 61-year-old woman, were injured in the crash.
Rengit Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Mohd Khairul Azmi Ngatman said the department received an emergency call at 8.01pm before six firefighters were dispatched to the scene.
He said the two injured victims were trapped in their vehicle before being extricated by firefighters using special equipment.
"The accident caused about 60 per cent of the Proton Saga BLM to catch fire. Based on witness accounts, two victims were trapped and burnt to death inside the vehicle.
"Firefighters carried out extinguishing operations using a hose reel, while an ambulance was also dispatched to provide treatment to the injured," he said.
The remains of both victims were later handed over to the police for further action.

Title: Selangor revenue hits RM3bil, surpasses target
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Selangor has recorded RM3 billion in revenue to date, surpassing the state's RM2.8 billion target set in its previous state budget, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
He said the achievement reflected the state's positive economic growth momentum and progress in implementing its development agenda.
"When I tabled the (state) budget on Nov 13, our revenue had reached RM2.95 billion, and yesterday it reached RM3 billion," he said at the 2026 Media Appreciation Ceremony organised by the Selangor Implementation Coordination Unit of the Prime Minister's Department here yesterday.
On another matter, Amirudin said the state government plans to improve people's living standards through a new approach that goes beyond existing poverty measurements.
He said although Selangor had achieved zero hardcore poverty, nearly 65,000 individuals remained registered in the eKasih system and required continued attention and assistance.
Amirudin said the state government was therefore formulating a decent living or dignified living approach to ensure that assistance provided could genuinely help lift people out of poverty.
"We are working to upgrade our poverty measurement to one based on quality of life, decent living or dignified living, as we intend to call it.
"We will name it in June, and the matter will be coordinated with the Implementation Coordination Unit while also taking into account the contexts of hardcore poverty and relative poverty," he said.
Amirudin said the approach aimed to establish a new framework for assessing people's actual needs, ensuring that assistance would not merely meet basic requirements but also help improve their quality of life.
He said the State Development Action Council is responsible not only for monitoring the implementation of large-scale development projects but also for addressing poverty and public welfare issues.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Floods hit 'flood mosque' in Kuala Selangor again
Article:
KUALA SELANGOR: Less than two weeks after it was last inundated, Masjid At-Taufiqiah in Bandar Seri Coalfields here, popularly known as the 'flood mosque', was hit by floods again tonight.
Mosque committee member Hasan Md Rasol, 62, confirmed the incident when contacted.
He said mosque management members immediately mobilised a clean-up and rescue effort after Isyak prayers to move items, including carpets, prayer mats and copies of the Quran, to safer locations.
"As at 9.40pm, floodwaters had covered almost the entire mosque compound.
"The electricity supply was also temporarily disconnected as a safety precaution," he said.
Hasan said the flooding was similar to the incident on Nov 4.
The mosque had previously been inundated by muddy floodwaters seven times, with the worst incident occurring in December 2021.

Title: Voter-roll deletions leave some Indian Muslims facing detention, deportation
Article:
WHEN   Sahida Fakir stepped out of her Mumbai home on July 19 to buy vegetables, she told her son she would be back in minutes.
More than three months later, the 38-year-old is living in a Bangladeshi village, separated from her husband and two sons.
Fakir said plainclothes officers detained her, seized her phone, which she said contained copies of identity documents, and forced her across the border.
Court filings show the officials belonged to the Mumbai police crime branch.
"Someone grabbed my hand from behind and ordered me to get into the vehicle," Fakir told Reuters in Satkhira, Bangladesh.
Fakir is among 10 families that Reuters interviewed whose relatives were detained, deported or questioned over their citizenship after being dropped from India's revised electoral rolls.
All had Indian identity or family documents while relatives, including parents and siblings, remain on the voter lists.
The cases show how India's sweeping voter-roll revision has become entangled with a separate drive to identify and expel suspected illegal immigrants, even though removal from the rolls does not itself establish that someone is a foreigner.
The voter list revision struck 130 million names nationwide in the largest deletion of voters in India's history.
Data shows the omissions disproportionately affect Muslims, India's largest minority, who have faced what rights groups describe as exclusionary policies and rising discrimination since Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) took power in 2014.
The revision sparked massive protests and accusations that the BJP was reshaping the electorate in its favour.
In West Bengal, where it has run furthest, around nine million names were cut ahead of state elections earlier this year.
Muslims made up about 70 per cent of the 2.7 million names deleted after a closer review, despite being 27 per cent of the population, according to the Kolkata-based Sabar Institute.
The BJP emerged victorious in those polls and took control of the state for the first time.
"We cannot deny the anti-incumbency factor, but the voter deletions played a big role in determining West Bengal election results," the institute's founder, Sabir Ahamed, said.
Fakir said she was pushed into Bangladesh at 1am from an unmanned, unfenced stretch of the border.
Now her husband, Jumman, is fighting her case in court, alongside millions of challenges to West Bengal's voter-roll revision.
Family records reviewed by Reuters show Fakir's parents and grandparents were registered voters in Swarupnagar, West Bengal, from India's first national election in 1952.
Their names also appeared on the 2002-2003 rolls, a benchmark in the latest revision for determining who could remain without submitting additional documents.
Fakir herself has appeared on West Bengal's electoral rolls since at least 2008, according to her voter ID seen by Reuters.
Mumbai's Foreigners Regional Registration Office told the Calcutta High Court that Fakir produced a Bangladeshi birth certificate during an inquiry and failed to produce "valid or credible documentary evidence" establishing Indian citizenship.
Fakir disputed that, saying authorities seized her phone and gave her no opportunity to show copies of documents stored on it.
Indian law does not require citizens to carry valid identification at all times.
In another petition before the Calcutta High Court, utensil hawker Nasiruddin Sheikh and four others said they were detained after their names were
removed from the rolls, even though appeals against deletion were pending before special tribunals.
Sheikh said police detained him and 22 others while he was working hundreds of kilometres from home in Chhattisgarh.
Nineteen people were released when authorities found their names on revised rolls. Sheikh and three others whose names did not appear remained in custody for 32 days.
"A policeman told me, 'your name is not in the voter list. You are a Bangladeshi'," Sheikh said.
He was released with the others the night before their court hearing.
At a holding centre for suspected foreign migrants in Murshidabad, Reuters reporters saw clothes hanging inside and people peering from windows.
"There are millions of cases against deletion of names from voter list and people are waiting for justice," human rights activist Kirity Roy said.
"The tribunals are slow. We are hopeless with what is going on."
The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump acknowledges Anwar's role in Cambodia-Thailand peace deal
Article:
MANILA: US President Donald Trump has acknowledged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's commitment and cooperation in securing the Kuala Lumpur Peace Accord between Cambodia and Thailand last year.
He said his cooperation with Anwar during last year's Asean Summit had resulted in a historic agreement that led to a ceasefire between the two countries.
Trump said Washington remained committed to upholding the ceasefire and ensuring the full implementation of the agreement.
"We remain committed to upholding that ceasefire and ensuring the full and effective implementation of the agreement as agreed a year ago," he said at the Asean-US Special Summit, held in conjunction with the 49th Asean Summit here today.
Trump also highlighted Malaysia as one of the countries that had signed trade agreements with Washington since he returned to office.
He said the United States had concluded several major agreements in the region covering energy, critical minerals and technology.
"Since I returned to office, we have concluded major trade agreements with Malaysia, Cambodia and Indonesia, as well as Japan, South Korea and almost every country represented at this table," he said.
He noted Southeast Asia's strategic importance in international trade, with about a quarter of the world's shipping traffic passing through the Strait of Malacca.
Trump said the United States was committed to strengthening economic ties with its regional partners and hoped to expand cooperation in critical minerals, rare earth elements and magnets.

Title: Brexit's old battle lines return as UK seeks EU reset
Article:
AS United Kingdom leader Andy Burnham prepares for a crunch European Union summit this week, familiar faces from Britain's Brexit wars are back, seeking to scupper his determination to forge closer ties to the bloc.
The Labour prime minister hopes to ink a reset with European chiefs in Brussels on Friday, cementing his pledge to secure a better relationship a decade after Britain voted to leave.
Ahead of the meeting, pro-Brexit voices from the 2016 vote are reorganising, concerned by Burnham's reset plans and flirting with the idea that Britain could one day seek to rejoin the EU.
In a speech late on Monday, the British leader, who replaced Keir Starmer in July, said Britain had left the bloc in 2020 on "bad terms" and needed "to consider whether the relationship we have now is right".
"It's like the emperor's new clothes where no one is prepared to say the obvious truth," he added, arguing "we have lost more than we have gained in the last 10 years".
"The hard Brexit we were given is not good enough for Britain," Burnham said, reiterating his criticism that it has made the country poorer and contributed to higher immigration.
He noted the summit would focus on securing three agreements:  cut red tape for food exports, link the two sides' emissions-trading schemes and finalise a "youth experience scheme".
But breaking with several years of taboo on the issue, Burnham suggested going further longer-term, pledging that post-summit London will "initiate a discussion with our EU partners about options" for the future relationship.
He added the talks "will take time" and he will present "options and our assessment of them to inform decisions in the next parliament" after the next general election, due by 2029.
"At every stage the British people will be the boss," he said.
His stance has been increasingly spooking Brexit's backers.
Ahead of the speech, former premier Boris Johnson — a key "leave" campaigner who later negotiated the terms of Britain's exit — told the
Telegraph
it was "madness" to reopen the debate.
He insisted the country would back Brexit again in another referendum — despite polls suggesting the opposite.
His comments echoed those of one of his predecessors, David Cameron, who as prime minister called the EU referendum, campaigned for Britain to stay and then resigned when he lost.
Last week, Cameron urged Burnham not to trigger a "decade-long debate" about rejoining the EU that he said would be "very long and painful".
Burnham has committed to his predecessor Starmer's "red lines" on Europe for this Parliament, meaning no return to the single market, customs union or freedom of movement.
But the issue has the potential to split his ruling centre-left Labour.
One party member of parliament said it should just "go for it" and put a commitment to rejoining in its manifesto for the next election.
However, some lawmakers in Brexit-supporting areas want Burnham to shut down the debate altogether, highlighting divisions within the ruling party, never mind the country.
Last week, one of Johnson's former Brexit advisers, Oliver Lewis, launched a new campaign called "Stay Out".
He said the UK leader will on Friday "sign a deal that sends more money to Brussels, hands back control of our own laws and opens the door to more immigration".
Meanwhile, the
Telegraph
reported that former pro-Brexit campaign group "Leave.EU" is planning to relaunch under the name "Enough Official".
"The UK really needs a debate about the world in 2026 rather than rehashing the same arguments from the same people as 10 years ago," said David Henig, an expert on UK-EU relations.
"Russia's invasion of Ukraine and Trump's attacks on world trade are obvious new factors that have happened since then.
"Meanwhile, the economic benefits promised have not materialised."
The writers are from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Queen arrives in Turkiye for COP31
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has arrived in Antalya, Turkiye, to attend the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31).
According to a post on the Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar Facebook page today, Her Majesty's special aircraft landed at Antalya Airport about 3pm local time (8pm Malaysian time).
Her Majesty was accompanied by Tunku Temenggong of Johor Tunku Idris Iskandar Sultan Ibrahim and was received upon arrival by Malaysian Ambassador to Turkiye Adlan Mohd Shaffieq and Turkish Foreign Ministry representative Ambassador Deha Erpek.
Her Majesty is scheduled to officiate at the closing of the Malaysia Pavilion and attend Johor Day at the pavilion, which will showcase the state's sustainability agenda and initiatives spearheaded by the Johor Sustainability Centre (JSC). - BERNAMA

Title: NST Leader: Malaysia must protect athletes after retirement
Article:
THERE are two positive outcomes for elite athletes once they retire: they take on roles in the sports system that made them great  or they exploit their fame and contacts to become entrepreneurs. On the flip side of the coin are those who have little to show for it after their glory days are over.
Possessing neither wealth nor recognition, they find themselves unable to shake off the extended funk of depression.   Like a former national squash champion who had been ranked 38th in the world, but by 2023, he was in ill health and depressed, working as a general cleaner for RM1,500 a month.
Or a former motorcycle racer who suffered memory loss, mobility issues and speech impairment after a racing incident.   In contrast, several former elite athletes ploughed their winnings and government  perks into sustainable entrepreneurship.
Others took up jobs in management and coaching, using their skills, experience and know-how to get on with the second act of their lives.
The squash and racing champions are but two  cases to illustrate the dramatic life changes after initial sporting success.
Over generations, Malaysia has produced countless world-class athletes. While we thank them for their service, it is also  time to repay the debt we owe them.
Concerns were raised by Datuk Azizulhasni Awang during a recent podcast episode with Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz, where the star cyclist pointed out  that many former  athletes suffered from depression and were  in need of guidance as they struggled to transition to life after competitive sports.
But he cautioned that what they needed was a "fishing rod, not handouts".    Years of training comes at the expense of education, injury, age or loss of form that ends lucrative careers.
To be sure, Malaysia has taken steps through organisations like the National Athletes' Welfare Foundation (Yakeb), which will see its allocation increased from RM1 million this year to RM2.5 million next year.
In the meantime, the current crop of athletes must be instructed in transition planning through a  programme covering education, vocational qualifications, financial literacy and a second-career pathway.    Preparation should intensify a few years before retirement by providing internships, job placements and coaching or sports-management qualifications.
Former athletes have  transferable skills: discipline, teamwork, resilience and the ability to perform under pressure.   They can contribute in administration, event operations, fitness, education and community development.
Their education should cover budgeting, debt, investment risks and irregular income.   Some athletes retire with injuries or disabilities that prevent them from working, so they should have financial protection, such as through  Employees' Provident Fund and Social Security Organisation  contributions.
Ultimately, athletes' welfare must not be judged by medals, fame or celebrity status.

Title: Sewerage sector could generate new revenue through circular economy, says Fadillah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The sewerage sector has the potential to drive the country's new circular economy through energy generation from biogas, the production of biosolid fertilisers, and the resupply of treated water to high-impact industries such as data centres.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said this approach not only optimises high-capacity sewage management but also has the potential to generate new revenue while supporting the nation's water resource sustainability.
Fadillah, who is also the energy transition and water transformation (Petra) minister, said that so far, fertiliser products derived from sewage biosolids produced by Indah Water Konsortium (IWK) Sdn Bhd have obtained halal certification and are being used in the agricultural sector, including vegetable farming.
"So these are part of the efforts we are making so that this recycle economy will help increase revenue," he said when speaking at the 2026 Petra Media Engagement Session here today.
Also present were Petra deputy secretary-general (water sector) Datuk Mohd Rodzwan Mohd Baba Sakri, Petra deputy secretary-general (energy sector) Datin Mareena Mahpudz, and Bernama news service deputy editor-in-chief Mohd Shukri Ishak.
Fadillah said under the 13th Malaysia Plan (RMK13), his ministry received an allocation totaling RM16.19 billion under the First Rolling Plan to implement overall water and sewerage sector development projects, including new and extension projects to enhance the technical capacity of the sector.
He noted that as of October 2024, the public sewerage asset portfolio managed by the Sewerage Services Department (JPP) is estimated to be worth RM22.69 billion, encompassing 7,618 sewage treatment plants, 1,443 pump stations, 24,024km of sewerage pipe networks, and 4,653 sewerage reserve land lots.
Commenting on the sector's challenges, Fadillah said the main focus now is connecting old premises and residential areas that still rely on individual septic tanks to a centralised sewerage system to prevent the risk of waste overflowing into drainage systems and rivers.
"Right now we have many septic tanks. We want, if possible, for all these septic tanks to be connected to the central sewerage system. It is more effective.
"Otherwise, we have to go to every septic tank, and sometimes homeowners do not want their septic tanks cleaned. In the end, the overflow or excess water will flow into drains and ditches, and eventually end up in the river," he said.
He said similar issues also involve houses of worship facing funding constraints for regular maintenance, prompting IWK to intensify corporate social responsibility (CSR) programmes to assist with the cleaning of sewerage systems at these premises.
Fadillah added that the government also faces challenges in rationalising and upgrading small-scale, outdated treatment plants that are no longer economical, alongside strengthening monitoring of effluent discharge standard compliance due to a limited number of enforcement officers.
Therefore, he said cooperation between the federal government, state governments, and local authorities must be strengthened in the planning and regulation of sewerage infrastructure to align with population growth and rapid industrial development.
At the same time, he called on media practitioners to continue playing the role of the government's eyes and ears in raising public awareness regarding the importance of scheduled septic tank desludging and channeling immediate information if they detect odor pollution or treatment plant malfunctions on the ground.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore takes over Asean chairship from Philippines for 2027
Article:
MANILA: The Philippines formally handed over the chairship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) to Singapore, concluding its year-long leadership of the regional bloc.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr led the turnover ceremony during the closing of the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits at the Philippine International Convention Centre in Pasay City.
Marcos said he was confident Singapore, as Asean chair in 2027, would lead with "a clarity of purpose, steadiness and commitment to regional cooperation".
"Today marks the ceremonial transition of the Asean chairship to Singapore for 2027. To Prime Minister (Lawrence) Wong and the people of Singapore, we have the utmost confidence. We offer our friendship and our full and complete support," he said.
"As one of Asean's founding members, Singapore has been a hand that has helped shape this community from creation. Its story reflects the value of openness, connection, discipline and cooperation. As Asean enters its 60th year, it is proper that Singapore should now take its helm."
With Singapore set to assume the chairship in 2027, Marcos reaffirmed the Philippines' commitment to actively participate in regional initiatives and support the incoming chair's priorities.
"Today, the helm passes from one chair to the next, and Asean's journey remains as it has ever been one that we travel together. Let us in Asean always be navigating our future together," Marcos said.
The turnover reaffirmed Asean's tradition of collective leadership and continuity in pursuing regional peace, stability and shared prosperity.
The handover marked the culmination of the Philippines' 2026 Asean chairship, anchored on the theme "Navigating Our Future, Together".
Lawrence Wong accepted the gavel from Marcos, signalling Singapore's assumption of the Asean chairship for 2027.
In his speech, Wong said Singapore would lead the regional bloc towards "deeper integration (and) wider partnerships" under its chairship.
"Deeper integration because we can do much more to realise the full potential of Asean. This includes strengthening our links in finance, digital technologies and energy," he said.
"Wider partnerships because Asean must continue to be open and outward-looking. At a time when the world is becoming more divided, our response is to keep building bridges, to strengthen ties with our partners, many of whom are here."
Under its leadership, the Philippines pursued three strategic priorities: peace and security anchors, prosperity corridors and people empowerment.
These priorities guided the country's initiatives to strengthen regional stability, promote economic integration and ensure that Asean cooperation translates into tangible benefits for its people.
Among the key areas advanced during the Philippine chairship were maritime cooperation, efforts to combat transnational crimes, digital economic integration, energy security and stronger regional connectivity.
The Philippines also pushed for progress in negotiations for a code of conduct in the South China Sea, which seeks to establish rules and mechanisms to prevent disputes from escalating.
Marcos earlier said that Asean's collective strength lies in the ability of its member states to work together despite their differences. - BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump hails 'victory' as US, Thailand sign trade statement
Article:
MANILA: US President Donald Trump and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul signed a joint statement on trade on Tuesday, with the American leader hailing a "victory for both countries" in ongoing negotiations.
A framework agreement was unveiled just over a year ago, on the same day Trump announced a short-lived ceasefire between Thailand and its neighbour Cambodia following deadly border clashes.
The United States is Thailand's largest export market, with the Southeast Asian nation recording a surplus of US$71.7 billion last year, according to US data.
"We're going to do a lot of trade," Trump told a news conference on the sidelines of a summit of leaders from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations in Manila.
"Thailand will eliminate all tariffs on US exports" and "remove substantial non-tariff barriers on American vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol, and poultry," Trump said.
Thailand will also buy "an estimated US$2.6 billion in additional US agricultural products", he added.
"This is an incredible victory for both countries."
Anutin said negotiators had "reached a substantial conclusion" in their talks on the final agreement on reciprocal trade.
"I am confident that the agreement will be ready for us to sign real soon," Anutin said.
In July, Washington imposed tariffs of 12.5 perc ent on imports from Thailand, one of dozens of countries targeted in an investigation into forced labour.
Thailand was also included this week among countries subject to new US export licences on advanced AI chips, intended to prevent Chinese firms from obtaining access to the technology.
Washington announced trade agreements with both Thailand and Cambodia at an Asean summit in October 2025, the same day Trump co-signed a ceasefire agreement.
The timing prompted speculation Trump had used US economic ties as leverage to try to end the conflict – one of several he says he has solved.
Long-running tensions over the border broke out into violence in July 2025, killing dozens of people.
Trump's truce proved short-lived, as fighting erupted again in December, although a ceasefire agreed since then has broadly held.
The 2025 framework trade agreement envisaged a 19-per cent baseline US tariff on Thai imports and the elimination of tariffs on nearly all US goods heading into Thailand.
The two sides also agreed a non-binding memorandum outlining increased cooperation on trading rare earth minerals, which are vital to tech products and of which China is the world's leading producer.
Trump has unleashed a barrage of tariffs on trading partners since last year.
Although the Supreme Court struck down country-specific tariffs in February, Washington has since alleged insufficient action against forced labour to slap new tariffs on 60 economies, including Thailand.
Separate duties targeting sectors like steel, autos and timber remain intact.--AFP

Title: Kepong parang attack: Injured policeman held fire to protect public, Bukit Aman reveals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A police Lance Corporal held his fire during a parang attack in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong,
on Nov 11
to protect bystanders from stray bullets, Bukit Aman said.
Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said the officer was entitled to defend himself against a life-threatening attack.
However, he said the officer feared that firing his weapon could endanger nearby members of the public through ricochets or bullet fragments, potentially worsening the situation.
"The officer took into account the surrounding circumstances and the risks to others before making his decision.
"He also believed that the firearm in his possession might deter the suspect from continuing his violent actions, but the suspect was not intimidated and continued attacking," he said after visiting the officer at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) today.
Deputy Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid and several senior officers were also present during the visit.
Noor Hisam said the 26-year-old officer had acted in accordance with police standard operating procedures (SOPs) during the emergency.
He said video footage showed the officer managed to maintain control of the situation and direct bystanders to seek shelter despite sustaining serious injuries.
During the Nov 11 incident, the officer was on duty at a house in Desa Aman Puri when a foreign national attacked him with a parang, severing his right wrist and injuring his head and body.
The suspect fled but was traced near a playground, where he again attacked the officer attempting to apprehend him.
Police opened fire in self-defence, and the suspect was pronounced dead while being taken to hospital.
On Nov 12, a team of HKL specialists
reattached
the officer's right wrist in an eight-hour operation.

Title: Wanted fraud suspect found hidden under luggage in car at Malaysia-Thailand border
Article:
KOTA BARU: A Thai man was arrested for allegedly smuggling a woman wanted in a fraud case from Malaysia into Thailand by concealing her beneath a pile of luggage in his vehicle.
A Thai security spokesman said the 39-year-old was driving a Toyota Fortuner when officers from the Sadao Immigration Department stopped him at the AC2 inspection lane of the new Sadao Immigration Complex at about 4.50pm yesterday.
The man failed to produce his passport, prompting officers to inspect the vehicle further.
"They then discovered the woman concealed beneath a pile of luggage, without any travel documents," the spokesman said.
Further checks found that the woman was wanted under a Nonthaburi Provincial Court arrest warrant dated Jan 22, 2025, over alleged conspiracy to defraud members of the public and offences involving the insertion of false information into computer systems, deposit accounts and electronic cards.
The spokesman said the man admitted to picking up the woman in Malaysia before bringing her into Thailand illegally.
Records also showed that he had been arrested twice previously for similar offences, including violations of the Immigration Act and assisting a person suspected of committing an offence to evade arrest.
Police seized the Toyota Fortuner as evidence before handing the suspect over to investigators at Sadao Police Station for further action.
Meanwhile, Thai Immigration Police Commissioner Lt Gen Nopsilp Poolsawat has directed the Songkhla Immigration Department to step up inspections of individuals and vehicles along the border.
The directive is in line with the policy of "Facilitating good people while making it difficult for criminals to evade checks", aimed at preventing offenders from using border routes to flee or evade legal action.

Title: Man who threatened Wisma Darul Aman guard with knife to be charged tomorrow
Article:
ALOR SETAR: A man arrested for trespassing into Wisma Darul Aman and pulling a knife on a security guard on Sunday will be charged at the Alor Setar Magistrate's Court tomorrow.
Kota Setar police chief Assistant Commissioner Syed Basri Syed Ali said the man would face two charges involving possession of a dangerous weapon in a public place and criminal trespass.
He said the charges would be brought under Section 6(1) of the Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Offensive Weapons Act 1958 and Section 447 of the Penal Code.
Earlier reports said the 45-year-old suspect
was arrested
after entering the Wisma Darul Aman compound without stopping at the security checkpoint before pulling a knife on a guard.
The incident occurred at about 8.10am when the suspect, riding a grey Yamaha Ego Gear scooter, allegedly entered the building's main entrance alone.
He then produced a small black knife and pointed it at the security guard before being apprehended and handed over to police.
A urine screening test found that the suspect was positive for methamphetamine and amphetamine.

Title: Widow recalls late policeman's unusual request for hot Nescafe
Article:
TAPAH: Lance Corporal Muhammad Shahrul Alif Yaacob's unusual request for hot Nescafe this morning became his wife's last memory of him before he was killed in a police van crash along the North-South Expressway (PLUS) today.
His wife, Nor Ilyanie Abd Aziz, 26, said she usually prepared iced Nescafe for him whenever he was on duty or travelling long distances.
"He would usually ask for Nescafe and whenever he had to travel far for duty, I would prepare some for him along with food.
"I had already made iced Nescafe, but he asked for it hot instead. I don't know why he wanted hot Nescafe this morning. He just said it was all right since I had already prepared the iced one," she said after funeral prayers at Surau Al-Ehsaniah, Tapah police housing complex, here today.
Recalling her husband, Nor Ilyanie described him as a kind and loving man who never neglected his responsibilities as a husband, father and son.
"He always took care of me, asking whether I had eaten and how things were at the office. Even when it was time to sleep, he would check on me.
"I often complained of back pain, so he would massage my back at night to make sure I could sleep comfortably," she said.
She said she learnt about the crash from his colleagues, who contacted her shortly after it happened about 11.30am.
The couple married on April 12, 2024 and had a six-month-old son.
Earlier, Muhammad Shahrul, attached to the Batu Gajah district police headquarters,
was killed
after being thrown from a police van carrying 11 personnel when it skidded at KM352 of the southbound expressway about 11.35am.
The 10 other in the van were injured, four seriously and six sustaining minor injuries.

Title: Six hurt after MMEA truck skids off road in Kelantan
Article:
KOTA BARU: Four Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) personnel and two undocumented migrants escaped with minor injuries after the truck they were travelling in skidded off the road near Peringat here today.
Kelantan MMEA director Maritime Captain Kamal Mohamad said the incident occurred at 11.30am in Padang Mokan.
He said the group was returning to the Kelantan Maritime State Headquarters in Tok Bali, Pasir Puteh, after attending a court hearing in Kota Baru.
"I was informed that the truck skidded off the road while trying to avoid a car that suddenly turned right," he said when contacted.
Kamal said the four MMEA personnel, comprising two men and two women, and the two detainees, both Bangladeshis, did not sustain serious injuries.
All six were taken to Hospital Universiti Sains Malaysia (HUSM) in Kubang Kerian for outpatient treatment.
He said the two detainees had since been discharged and were being held at the lock-up at the Kelantan Maritime State Headquarters.

Title: Israel set to elect Netanyahu opponent as parliament speaker
Article:
JERUSALEM: Israel's parliament is set Tuesday to select a new speaker opposed to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, a first step in rolling back the legacy of the country's divisive veteran leader even though he is still trying to stay in office.
Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief who has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu, has put forward his ally Matan Kahana to be the next speaker.
Netanyahu's Likud party is expected to try to draw out debate to scuttle Kahana's election in the parliament, known as the Knesset.
Likud in a statement demanded that lawmakers hold off on "severe, unilateral measures" and on "replacing the Knesset speaker at a time that negotiations are ongoing to form a national-unity government."
Likud has said it will put forward Ofir Katz as its own candidate for Knesset speaker, but Kahana is the favourite ahead of the vote.
The parliament speaker is an important office given that it sets the timetable for parliamentary business and can therefore speed up or delay debates or votes on proposed laws.
Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu won a majority in the 120-member Knesset in Oct 27 elections.
But Kahana can easily reach the 61-vote threshold in Tuesday's vote thanks to votes by the Arab-Israeli parties, which made historic gains in the election on the back of anger over Netanyahu's hard-right government.
Netanyahu's and Eisenkot's parties met Sunday on the possibility of joining a unity government but the meeting appeared to be largely a formality, with both men saying they should be prime minister.
Netanyahu, who has been urging US President Donald Trump to resume war on Iran, has talked up the threat from Tehran as he insists on the need for a unity government.
Eisenkot said afterwards that Netanyahu was unfit to "remain at the helm of government for even one more minute" after an explosive media report that his allies tried to make up allegations of fraud to frame lawmakers from the Arab minority.
- TARGETING NETANYAHU ERA -
If Kahana takes charge, he is expected as soon as Wednesday to start the process of undoing much of the agenda of Netanyahu, Israel's longest serving prime minister who has been in and out of office for three decades.
The new parliament is expected first to move to rescind sweeping reforms to reduce the independence of the judiciary that were advanced by Netanyahu, who has been enraged over corruption charges against him that could land him in prison if he loses power.
The judicial reforms initiated shortly after Netanyahu began his latest term in December 2022 triggered some of Israel's largest ever protests, bringing tens of thousands to the streets, with liberals fearing an erosion of the country's democracy.
The movement was eventually overshadowed on Oct 7, 2023 when Hamas carried out the deadliest attack ever against Israel, which responded with a relentless retaliatory offensive in Gaza.
Eisenkot has also vowed to quickly set up a state commission of inquiry to investigate security failures that led to the Oct 7 attack.
Netanyahu, who has built his brand on saying he will ensure Israel's security, has refused an independent probe, instead proposing one whose members would be chosen by politicians.
Kahana, 54, like Eisenkot is a veteran military leader. He served in a short-lived non-Netanyahu government in 2021 and 2022 as minister for religious services in which he clashed with ultra-Orthodox Jews by seeking to reduce the power of the Chief Rabbinate.
Kahana himself is religious, part of Eisenkot's efforts to form a broad coalition that ranges from secular liberals to religious conservatives.
Eisenkot's efforts to form a coalition have focused on wooing the ultra-Orthodox, historic allies of Netanyahu, after Liberman dropped his signature, longtime demand that the community serve in the military.
Religious students are exempt from Israel's mandatory military service, fuelling resentment at a time that reservists are stretched by multiple wars.--AFP

Title: Esscom officer's wife claims she was stripped, assaulted during police questioning
Article:
TAWAU: The High Court here was told today that the wife of an Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esscom) officer was allegedly forced to strip naked and assaulted by investigators while being questioned over the January 2023 murder of e-hailing driver Nurman Bakaratu.
Vivien Fabian, 38, the 14th plaintiff's witness, testified that a female officer from Bukit Aman had ordered her to remove her clothes one by one before making her squat facing a wall for several minutes in an interrogation room at the Tawau district police headquarters.
Under further questioning by lead counsel Datuk Ram Singh, Vivien alleged that another male officer covered her eyes with a face mask before slapping both her ears.
Asked whether she had complied with the order to remove her clothes, Vivien said she had stripped completely before being instructed to squat facing the wall.
She said she did not know why she was ordered to do so, but believed the officers wanted her to confess to involvement in the murder.
Vivien also alleged that the female officer had struck her back 10 to 15 times while pressuring her to admit being at the murder scene, which was an oil palm plantation.
She said she refused to confess, maintaining that she and her husband were in Lahad Datu on Jan 13, 2023, including at a food stall, and were not at the scene.
She further claimed that investigators had used her three children to exert psychological pressure on her during her detention, including bringing them to the Tawau police headquarters and allowing her to see them through tinted glass.
Vivien was seen crying several times while testifying about the alleged abuse and matters involving her children. Several family members following the proceedings from the public gallery were also visibly emotional.
During cross-examination by senior federal counsel Mardziatun Nisa Ahmadul Kaber, Vivien agreed that her police report detailing the alleged physical abuse was lodged only on April 28, 2023, about three months after the incident.
However, she disagreed that the report was an afterthought or that her allegations, including being forced to strip, had been fabricated to support the civil suit.
She also agreed that she did not know the names or ranks of the two officers involved, but disputed the suggestion that the male officer had not been in the room or had never touched or assaulted her.
Mardziatun further suggested that the allegations of assault, forced stripping and the use of her children were fabricated and exaggerated to support the multimillion-ringgit civil claim.
Vivien disagreed, adding that she would leave it to the judge to assess the allegations when questioned about the absence of medical reports documenting her injuries.

Title: Asean, China reaffirm South China Sea declaration pending code of conduct
Article:
MANILA: Asean and China remain committed to the Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea until a long-awaited code of conduct is finalised, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr said on Tuesday.
"There was a tacit agreement that we will abide by the declaration," Marcos told reporters after the close of the Asean summit in Manila.
"Until the code of conduct is ready, until it is finalised and signed by all parties, by Asean and China have pledged to follow the declaration's guidance."
Marcos said Asean and China had reaffirmed their commitment to complete negotiations on a substantive and effective code of conduct consistent with the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.
Asean and China have failed to conclude negotiations on the code during the Philippines' stint as chair of the bloc.--REUTERS

Title: Ahmad Yakob appointed new Pas Mursyidul Am
Article:
ALOR SETAR: Former Kelantan menteri besar Datuk Ahmad Yakob has been appointed the new Mursyidul Am of Pas, replacing Datuk Hashim Jasin.
The Pas Syura Ulama Council also appointed Johor Pas commissioner Datuk Dr Mahfodz Mohamed as deputy Mursyidul Am, while Demit assemblyman Mohd Asri Mat Daud was named the council's new secretary.
Pas central Ulama Wing chief Datuk Ahmad Yahaya said the party appreciated Hashim's contributions, sacrifices and commitment throughout his tenure since 2016.
He expressed hope that the newly appointed leadership would continue strengthening the council's role in guiding Pas' struggle based on the Quran and Sunnah.
"The Pas Syura Ulama Council records its deepest appreciation and gratitude to Tuan Guru Datuk Hashim Jasin for his services and contributions throughout his tenure as Mursyidul Am.
"Similar appreciation is extended to Datuk Nik Muhammad Zawawi Salleh for his services and dedication in carrying out his responsibilities as secretary of the Pas Syura Ulama Council," he said in a statement tonight.
Ahmad, who is also Pokok Sena member of parliament, said this in a statement issued here.
Hashim had previously experienced health problems and received treatment at Hospital Tuanku Fauziah in Kangar from February before being transferred to Penang Hospital.
His condition was later reported to have stabilised, and he was allowed to return home in March after showing positive progress.
Hashim was appointed the fourth Mursyidul Am of Pas on Oct 10, 2016, by the Pas Syura Ulama Council, succeeding the late Datuk Dr Haron Din, who died on Sept 16 that year.

Title: Macron's visit puts Rafale back in Malaysia's MRCA fight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: France's Rafale fighter jet is among the options being assessed as Malaysia explores its future combat aircraft requirements, following discussions to deepen defence cooperation between Kuala Lumpur and Paris.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the
aircraft was among several proposals
discussed during his bilateral meeting with French Minister for the Armed Forces and Veterans Affairs Catherine Vautrin at Wisma Perwira ATM earlier today.
The discussions also covered the procurement of combat search and rescue helicopters, 105mm artillery systems and future submarine requirements.
Other areas included logistics support, modernisation of existing assets and greater involvement of local defence industries through technology transfer and expertise development, Khaled said in a Facebook post.
Earlier, French President Emmanuel Macron said France was looking to expand its s
trategic presence in Malaysia
through potential cooperation involving submarines, fighter jets and liquefied natural gas.
"We signed some agreements this morning for defence and security, including fighter jets, submarines ... we want to go more on LNG," he said in his keynote address at the France-Malaysia Business Forum 2026.
On Nov 12, Defence Ministry secretary-general Datuk Lokman Hakim Ali also received a courtesy call from French Ambassador to Malaysia Marc Abensour and a delegation from Dassault Aviation, the manufacturer of the Rafale.
The meeting touched on the potential Multi-Role Combat Aircraft (MRCA) replacement programme, with the French delegation presenting the capabilities and technology of the Rafale.
The twin-engine, multirole fighter is designed for air superiority, air defence, ground attack, reconnaissance and anti-ship missions. It can operate from land bases and aircraft carriers and carry various weapons, including air-to-air missiles, precision-guided bombs and long-range cruise missiles.
The aircraft is operated by the French Air and Space Force and Navy, as well as several foreign air forces, including Indonesia.
In September, Royal Malaysian Air Force chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris told the New Straits Times that
future fighter requirements
should be guided by Malaysia's defence needs and ability to protect its sovereignty and airspace, rather than simply pursuing the most advanced technology.
He also said the RMAF was reassessing conventional approaches to fighter fleet size, prioritising operational capabilities over the number of aircraft acquired.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three men nabbed in cable theft attempt in Taman Seri Sentosa
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Three men were arrested after police found them inside a utility manhole during an operation to investigate an attempted cable theft in Taman Seri Sentosa here yesterday.
The arrests followed a viral video on Threads showing one of the suspects being detained inside a manhole along Jalan Seri Sentosa.
Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said the operation began at 4pm after police received public information about suspicious activities at the location.
"A team from the Petaling police station task force, assisted by other police personnel, inspected the location and found two men inside the utility manhole.
"Both men were arrested, and police seized eight items, including cable cutters and an electric-powered cable pulling device, to facilitate investigations," he said in a statement today.
Hoo said police returned to the location at 7.30pm for further checks.
"With assistance from the Fire and Rescue Department and Telekom Malaysia, water was pumped out of the manhole.
"Police then discovered another man inside and arrested him," he said.
All three suspects and the seized equipment were taken to the Petaling police station for further action.
Hoo said the case was being investigated under Section 379, read together with Section 511 of the Penal Code, for attempted theft.
Investigations are ongoing to determine each suspect's role, verify ownership of the cables and establish whether any damage or financial losses were incurred.
He thanked members of the public for providing information that led to the arrests.
Those with information on the case can contact Brickfields police at 03-22979222 or visit the nearest police station.

Title: Make health insurance mandatory for UNHCR-registered refugees, govt urged
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government should require all refugees registered with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to have health insurance, to ease the financial burden on public healthcare facilities.
Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) said UNHCR should take responsibility for refugees issued with its cards by ensuring they were insured when seeking treatment at government hospitals and clinics.
"If they are so clever at giving out cards and allowing them in, then take responsibility and provide insurance," he said when debating the Health Ministry's allocation under the Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Radzi cited a written parliamentary reply from Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail yesterday, which showed that registered refugees increased from 125,493 in December 2025 to 133,400 as at Sept 30.
He said the increase of 7,907 occurred despite the Cabinet's July 23 directive for UNHCR to temporarily stop registering new refugees.
Citing the Auditor-General's Report 2/2026, Radzi said unpaid medical bills in 2025 totalled RM336 million, of which RM281 million was owed by non-citizens.
He questioned the effectiveness of the Health Ministry's "collect before discharge" approach, saying some foreign patients were allowed to leave without settling their bills when hospitals needed beds.
Radzi said mandatory insurance could also encourage UNHCR to expedite refugee resettlement in third countries, and called for the Health, Home and Foreign ministries to discuss the proposal.
In a separate written reply yesterday, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was studying sustainable
financing options for refugees and asylum seekers,
including mandatory health insurance.
The Cabinet's July directive to
suspend new registrations
was intended to restructure refugee management under government supervision.
Doctors Without Borders subsequently called for safeguards, warning that the move could deter undocumented refugees from
seeking healthcare.

Title: Trump, Thai PM to announce trade progress, not final deal
Article:
BANGKOK: US President Donald Trump will sign a joint statement with Thailand's premier on Tuesday marking "significant progress" in trade negotiations, but will not ink a final deal, a Thai official said.
A framework agreement was unveiled just over a year ago, on the same day as Trump announced a short-lived ceasefire between Thailand and its neighbour Cambodia following deadly border clashes.
The United States is Thailand's largest export market, with the Southeast Asian nation recording a surplus of US$71.7 billion last year, according to US data.
In July, Washington imposed new tariffs of 12.5 per cent on imports from Thailand, among dozens of countries targeted in an investigation into forced labour concerns.
Thailand was also included this week among countries subject to new US export licences on advanced AI chips, intended to prevent Chinese firms from obtaining access to the technology.
Trump and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul will make the joint statement on Tuesday at a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) in the Philippines, a Thai government official said.
Deputy spokeswoman Lalida Persvivatana told AFP it marked "significant progress" in negotiations on an agreement on reciprocal trade (ART).
"However, the signing is not yet the formal ART agreement," she said, noting Thailand still needed to conduct a public consultation and legal procedures.
The US had announced trade agreements with both Thailand and Cambodia at an Asean summit in October 2025, the same day as Trump co-signed a ceasefire agreement.
The timing prompted speculation Trump had used US economic ties as leverage to try to end the conflict – one of several he says he has solved.
Long-running tensions over the border broke out into violence in July 2025, killing dozens of people.
Trump's truce proved short-lived as fighting erupted again in December, although a ceasefire agreed since then has broadly held.
The 2025 framework trade agreement envisaged a 19-per cent baseline US tariff on Thai imports and the elimination of tariffs on nearly all US goods heading into Thailand.
The two sides also agreed a non-binding memorandum outlining increased cooperation on trading rare earth minerals, which are vital to tech products and of which China is the world's leading producer.
Trump has unleashed a barrage of tariffs on trading partners since last year.
Although the Supreme Court struck down country-specific tariffs in February, Washington has since alleged insufficient action against forced labour to slap new tariffs on 60 economies, including Thailand.
Separate duties targeting sectors like steel, autos and timber remain intact.--AFP

Title: SC unveils Sukuk Prisma for climate adaption and resilience
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) today introduced Sukuk Prisma to the global market, a new purpose-driven sustainable sukuk framework designed to mobilise capital for climate adaptation and resilience, supporting wider sustainable development priorities.
In a statement, the SC said the framework expands the capital market's scope beyond conventional green and social categories to encompass broader climate adaptation, resilience and transitional financing, including flood mitigation, coastal protection, agriculture and the resilience of power grids.
"It also supports sukuk issuances denominated in ringgit and major hard currencies, enabling access to international capital and connecting global investors with high-impact sustainable investment opportunities," it said.
Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup launched the Sukuk Prisma at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye.
Meanwhile, SC chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi said: "The framework introduces a broader and clearer thematic classification to support national sustainability agenda, making it more investable, enhances investor understanding and strengthens Malaysia's position as a leader in sustainable and Islamic finance."
The SC will issue the Sukuk Prisma Framework in the first quarter of 2027. Ahead of its issuance, the SC will undertake engagements with issuers, investors and other market participants to support market readiness and encourage early adoption.
